source.title: A Neural Chronometry of Memory Recall

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed review integrating human electrophysiology into a temporally ordered retrieval sequence: cue processing reaches medial temporal structures, hippocampal pattern completion begins, and target-specific cortical reinstatement follows. This supports the weaker MECH-547 principle that the active query/cue state governs which stored information is exposed and when. It does not distinguish receiver-conditioned translation from hippocampal indexing/pattern completion, so confidence is moderate rather than high.
failure_signatures: A future REE result in which a fixed sender-only retrieval cue reproduces T(A,B) performance would fit this literature without supporting receiver-state conditioning.
If translated content can be injected at arbitrary phases with equal effect, the temporally structured biological analogue becomes less relevant.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Human electrophysiological evidence supports a retrieval sequence in which cues engage hippocampal pattern completion followed by target-memory reinstatement in cortex over a structured time course.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports query/state-dependent exposure of stored information and reinforces the need to include temporal state in an interface assay. It is consistent with MECH-547 but also with simpler indexing/pattern-completion rivals.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review does not measure representational bridge complexity or explicitly compare fixed versus receiver-conditioned mappings.
mapping.source_context: Review of human memory-retrieval electrophysiology and fMRI with emphasis on temporal dynamics.

confidence_components.notes: Strong retrieval evidence; only adjacent to the exact artificial-interface claim.
